Current canonical navigation — updated 21 November 2026. This original compendium is preserved as a legacy/reference hub, not the complete source for the latest worldbuilding. For current revisions use Eryndor Compendium — Edition II (Provisional Audit, 20 Nov 2026), especially 03 — History & Ancient Lore. The comprehensive Second Age Annals — Historical Framework & Complete Culture Index (1–1437) and Era of Fire — Kingdoms, Peoples & Cultural Chronicle (Second Age, 1322–1437) contain the newly authorized detailed history. Current continuity snapshot: The Second Age lasted 1,437 years. Awakening, Wonder and Fire are Avarran era names only; other continents may divide or name time differently. Orcs existed in neither First nor Second Age: exiled dark mages of southeastern Avarra created them sometime during the Third Age, seeking ultimately to attack Khazari, Eldar and human kingdoms. The Third Age's proposed 8,873 years and nine Avarran eras remain a working framework. Current Fifth Age demographic model: approximately 2,062.8 million people worldwide, including 144 million Khazari, with Karak-Varn 22.8 million (the 3.8-million figure is a superseded legacy baseline). Historical accounts and local inventions in newer annals remain creator-revisable; they do not prove modern kingdom origins or reveal Gloin Hammerfeld's ancestry. Gloin's campaign is paused as before. A structured, expandable reference for the world of Eryndor and the ongoing campaign of Gloin Hammerfeld. This hub links the separate canon pages so that geography, peoples, history, magic, politics, creatures, characters and campaign mechanics can grow independently without turning into one enormous document. Primary source during reconstruction: The Eryndor World Bible. It is retained as a reference, not as the new master document. New pages should be checked against it and against the campaign's established continuity before canon is recorded. ## Canon status and evidence rules - Established canon: Directly established by the campaign, agreed worldbuilding, or reliable in-world evidence. - Reported: Something an NPC, witness, document or faction has claimed, but which has not been independently confirmed. - Hypothesis: A possible explanation or interpretation. It must not silently become fact. - Disputed: Accounts or traditions conflict, and the setting has no settled answer. - Unknown / open: Intentionally unresolved. Do not fill gaps simply because an answer would be convenient. - Current canon: The accepted version of Eryndor at this moment. The creator may revise, replace or retcon any element at any time. The nine additional peoples (Kobolds, Satyrs/Fauns, Pixies, Minotaurs, Brownies/Boggarts, Ogres, Trolls, Mushroom folk and Harpies) are established canon; their unresolved details remain open where explicitly identified as unknown. ## Compendium index The following reference pages are being built and audited against the original World Bible. The campaign chronicle is kept separate so dated events cannot be confused with general world lore. 1. World foundations and geography — cosmology, continents, regions, settlements, climate, travel scales and maps. 2. Peoples and cultures — established peoples, human cultures, sentient animal peoples, reputations, customs and social variation. The nine additional peoples are established canon and are documented in Peoples & Cultures. 3. History and ancient lore — ages, civilisations, the First Throne, ancient events, timelines, ruins and independent mysteries. 4. Magic and the cosmos — Natural Magic, lunar disciplines, satellites, compatibility, runecraft, Deepcraft and ancient harmonisation. 5. Technology, craft and infrastructure — high-medieval baseline, Khazari engineering, machinery, metallurgy, transport and the Deepways. 6. Politics, factions and institutions — thrones, kingdoms, rulers, noble houses, guilds, religion, military institutions, diplomacy and dissent. 7. Creatures and the natural world — ordinary wildlife, magical creatures, monsters, dragons, Ents, Giants and Living Mountains, including the nine additional peoples now established as canon. 8. Characters, families and relationships — established biographies, personal histories, relationships and NPC knowledge boundaries. 9. Visual canon and reference collection — approved character appearances, portrait references and visual production rules. 10. Economy, trade and material life — currency, prices, trade goods, wages, costs of living, accounting and economic variation. 11. Campaign rules and play systems — player agency, time, combat, training, progression, reputation, NPC autonomy, consequences and world simulation. 12. Open mysteries and research leads — a cross-reference of unanswered questions, evidence, competing explanations and who is investigating what. 13. Campaign chronicle — the chronological record of Gloin's journey. This page is created after the general canon references. ## Global continuity rules - Eryndor is a living world, but it advances only when campaign time passes. No background simulation occurs while the player is away or while the campaign is paused. - Gloin Hammerfeld is not a chosen one and has no secret lineage or guaranteed destiny. He has no plot armour; injury, failure, loss and death are possible consequences. - The player alone chooses Gloin's speech, decisions and actions. Never invent Gloin's dialogue, thoughts, intentions or unchosen actions. - NPCs have independent motives, knowledge, loyalties, temperaments and lives. They only know what has been disclosed to them or what they could reasonably discover. - Keep exact chronology, locations, object identities, money, inventory, commitments and scene continuity. Never invent purchases, payments, travel, training or elapsed time. - Distinguish observation from interpretation. Keep rumours, hypotheses, disputed accounts and unknowns visibly separate from established facts. - Species and cultural archetypes are reputations and tendencies, not biological laws or universal personalities. No people are inherently good, evil, foolish or uncivilised. Current canon remains binding until the creator explicitly revises or retcons it; future revisability does not make today's canon tentative. - New canon should be added to the correct reference page. Dated events belong in the Campaign Chronicle, not in general lore, except when a concise cross-reference is necessary. - When a new detail conflicts with older material, do not silently overwrite it. Record the discrepancy and resolve it against the user's latest explicit correction or decision. ## Source and reconstruction method The original World Bible is the first reference source. The ongoing conversation and retained campaign continuity are additional sources. During reconstruction, details are checked for status and date; newer, more precise campaign facts take precedence over older summaries when they clearly supersede them. Uncertain details remain marked as uncertain. Working master: This Compendium.
Historical reference: The original Eryndor World Bible, linked above.
Chronicle policy: Build only after the reference pages are complete, then verify its timeline and exact pause point before play resumes. [Magic & the Cosmos](https://app.notion.com/p/41ea4939d371819a9865eaabfe65453b) Technology, Craft & Infrastructure [Technology, Craft & Infrastructure](https://app.notion.com/p/41ea4939d371812686b5c08122319bae) Politics, Factions & Institutions [Politics, Factions & Institutions](https://app.notion.com/p/41ea4939d37181379a81cd1c7b6ab6e0) Economy, Trade & Material Life [Economy, Trade & Material Life](https://app.notion.com/p/41ea4939d3718152b182f1d7bb1048b7) Creatures & the Natural World [Creatures & the Natural World](https://app.notion.com/p/41ea4939d37181f39a3ade3c911eab8e) Characters, Families & Relationships [Characters, Families & Relationships](https://app.notion.com/p/41ea4939d371817a974fe21b6dcac140) [Visual Canon & Reference Collection](https://app.notion.com/p/41ea4939d37181e1a63cc646867d0d32) Campaign Rules & Play Systems [Campaign Rules & Play Systems](https://app.notion.com/p/41ea4939d371814fab3fce0fd1a313fa) Open Mysteries & Research Leads [Open Mysteries & Research Leads](https://app.notion.com/p/41ea4939d37181da82e7ee0f57077f7c) Campaign Chronicle — Gloin Hammerfeld [Campaign Chronicle — Gloin Hammerfeld](https://app.notion.com/p/41ea4939d3718198b93ccd0a86f901b4) Visual Canon & Reference Collection ## Reconstruction and continuity audit — completed The Compendium is the active working master. The original Eryndor World Bible is preserved as the historical source. The reference chapters and Campaign Chronicle have been compared against the original source and the retained campaign record. The campaign chronicle was checked last, including its exact scene pause, state ledger, outstanding commitments and knowledge boundaries. ### Canon is revisable; unresolved status still matters Everything in Eryndor is subject to the creator's revision, expansion, replacement or retcon at any time. “Established canon” means the current accepted version, not an immutable or untouchable one. A later explicit creator decision takes precedence and should be applied consistently across every affected chapter and the campaign record. The nine additional peoples—Kobolds, Satyrs/Fauns, Pixies, Minotaurs, Brownies/Boggarts, Ogres, Trolls, Mushroom folk and Harpies—are now established canon. Their current concepts, descriptions, cultural directions, encounter concepts and ecological notes are accepted as part of Eryndor. Specific details explicitly left unknown, unresolved or hypothetical remain so until developed in play or decided by the creator. A detail's inclusion in canon does not make every in-world rumour or hypothesis true. ### Audit findings and corrections - The five unapproved names accidentally introduced during the first reconstruction—Talarin, Khevari, Nerathi, Thallin and Cindari—remain excluded. They are not Eryndor canon. - The original Visual Canon & Reference Collection is transferred to [Visual Canon & Reference Collection](https://app.notion.com/p/41ea4939d37181e1a63cc646867d0d32). - All substantive original World Bible subject areas have destinations in the Compendium: foundations and geography; peoples and cultural archetypes; history and ancient discoveries; magic and celestial systems; technology and infrastructure; politics, military affairs, religion, dissent and wider society; economy and material life; creatures and wildlife; characters and family; visual canon; campaign rules; mysteries and research leads; and the chronological campaign record. - Restored source details include the First Throne listening-station diagram and old-quarry marker evidence; the attunement mark and Hammer and Crown authority seal; Dorin Blackmantle's dated Crownward entry and missing restricted assessment; Varric Stonehelm's role and the three distinct repository-register entries; the mine-inspection equipment list; planned inspection personnel versus recorded attendance; Gloin's earlier controlled aptitude tests; campaign-era political reports and rumours; and the fuller dissent and everyday-institution frameworks. - The nine additional peoples have since been promoted from development proposals to established canon by explicit creator decision. Their current concepts and ecological notes are accepted; explicitly unresolved details remain open to future development. - The creator's retroactive canon decision is that Gloin was 42 and Tovin 34 from the campaign's first scene on Autumn Day 19; Tovin is Gloin's younger brother. The opening-age misstatement was corrected in the canonical World Bible and should not be retained as an alternate character history. - A repeated “Earlier controlled aptitude tests” section was removed from the character page. The complete information remains in the primary aptitude section; no unique test result or training caveat was discarded. - Repeated repository details in the mystery register and campaign chronology are retained only where each serves a distinct purpose: the chronicle records what happened in sequence; the mystery register tracks the evidence, interpretation limits and outstanding lead. Do not create further verbatim copies when updating either page. - The currency reference intentionally supersedes the original source's two-denomination limit. The current standard is 100 copper = 1 silver, 100 silver = 1 gold and 100 gold = 1 platinum. Gloin's historical purse remains recorded in silver and copper. - The planned mine-inspection roster and the recorded attendance on Day 22 differ. The plan and actual attendance are both retained as separate facts; the source does not explain the change, so no reason has been invented. - Other mysteries remain intentionally unresolved: the nature of the eastern mine, the western wall, the drainage stone, the missing authority piece, the repository's contents, Veyron's motives, the King's actual knowledge and any relationship between distant sites. Their uncertainty is not a documentation defect. ### Cross-reference and maintenance rules - General world rules belong in their subject chapter. Dated events, player decisions, exact dialogue, inventory changes, money changes, time passage and campaign state belong in the Campaign Chronicle. - The Open Mysteries page is the evidence and lead register; it should summarise the issue and link to the chronicle for the full dated sequence rather than copying entire event passages. - Character biographies hold stable identity, relationships and long-term development. The chronicle holds the current state at a particular date. Update both when a campaign event changes a character's status. - Peoples & Cultures is the primary reference for the nine additional peoples' concepts and reputation spectrum. Creatures & the Natural World holds their ecological canon. Do not repeat the same full material across both pages. - Visual Canon holds approved visual references and production rules; do not treat an unapproved visual concept as an approved appearance. - When the user changes canon, update every affected reference and the current campaign ledger, then check for stale duplicates and contradictions. ### Final campaign verification The Campaign Chronicle ends at the verified pause point: Autumn, Day 22, Year 3,847, approximately 11:25 AM, at Hadrik Ironvein's desk in the Royal Historical Archive, Karak-Varn. Hadrik has asked Gloin and Maela what they have uncovered. Gloin has not answered. The state ledger records Gloin's condition, funds, inventory, training, commitments, research assignments and NPC knowledge boundaries. No time or events advance while paused. The chronicle is the final chronological campaign record. Do not write future events or resume the scene until the user chooses Gloin's response. ### Remaining open by design The audit is complete as a source-reconstruction and continuity pass. This does not mean every in-world question has an answer. Geographic precision, unnamed settlements, unknown histories, disputed accounts and active mysteries remain open wherever the source leaves them open. The nine additional peoples are established canon; their explicitly unresolved details remain available for future development and revision.
